subject: Control plane / network isolation: proposed bench & next tests
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmebank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed bench for control-plane & network isolation tests

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the tests we discussed so we have alignment before scheduling lab time: 

1) Goal: validate that Redwood Private (VPC + optional on-prem control plane) can meet Acme's network isolation and control-plane latency requirements while remaining compatible with your KMS/HSM and audit constraints.

2) Scope of the bench (what we proposed):
   - Network isolation: 2 modes — (A) VPC-control-plane (our control plane managed in Redwood account but peered to Acme, vetted network ACLs); (B) On-prem control plane (customer-managed, air-gapped with one-way sync). We will run connectivity and egress verification in both modes.
   - Control-plane latency: measure API round trips for model management operations (deploy, rollback, health-checks) across the control plane path and compare to hyperscaler-managed endpoints.
   - Failure/fallback behavior: simulate a model-serving region outage and verify automatic fallback to a pinned local model variant.

3) Success criteria (draft):
   - No unexpected external egress from data planes during isolation tests (packet-level checks + flow logs).
   - Control-plane round-trip median < 120ms for management operations in VPC mode (target; we can tighten).
   - Key management operations validated with your KMS (rotate, fetch) without exposing plaintext keys to Redwood-managed control plane in On-prem mode.

Next steps we agreed on:
- You to confirm which control-plane mode to prioritize for the first run (VPC-control-plane vs on-prem).
- Redwood to supply a detailed test plan and an isolation-test bundle (attached) for your security team to review.
- If agreed, we schedule a 2-day window for the bench (2 engineers from Acme + 2 Redwood SREs).

Attachments: isolation-test-design.pdf (high-level steps), controlplane-latency-sim.csv (sample baseline numbers).

If that matches your read, we can aim to lock a date next week.

Thanks —
Hannah

Hi Sarah / team —

Thanks for the questions — confirming the plan and a few implementation details we will run in the VPC-control-plane bench: 

1) Egress IPs: we will allocate a static CIDR (two /29s) and publish the IPs 48 hours before the run. These will be applied at the NAT/gateway level so management traffic from the control plane to your VPC uses only those IPs.

2) Packet capture: Redwood SRE will run tcpdump on an EC2 mirror instance that peers to your VPC mirror (or container equivalent). We will share encrypted pcap and a short summary of flows. We will also export flow logs (ENI + VPC Flow Logs) for cross-correlation.

3) Control-plane latency: realistic median for our VPC-control-plane path (management operations) measured in prior customers is ~80–110ms depending on region and peering setup. 120ms is safe for a starting SLO for the bench; we will run baseline measurements before the main test window to capture variability. For hyperscaler endpoints, management ops were ~60–90ms in our benchmarks but note those often trade off different routing/topology assumptions.

4) KMS/HSM: for the test we will use your test key via KMIP/CloudHSM bridge. We will not persist private key material; only ciphertext/CEKs are stored. We will provide an attestation flow and logs of KMS calls for audit.

Proposed timeline (all times PDT):
- Day -2: exchange egress IPs & service accounts; security sign-off on test plan.
- Day -1: baseline runs (10 minutes of synthetic mgmt ops + flow logging).
- Day 0 (test day): Isolation checks (packet capture + flow log analysis) and latency bench (4 hours).
- Day +1: post-run artifact delivery and debrief.

If that works, Hannah/Ben — let's propose two candidate weeks (Nov 2 or Nov 9) and lock people. Sarah — let me know which week works for your cross-functional team.

Thanks —
